merger_name: Aula Energy – Additional interest in the Boulder Creek Wind Farm
merger_description:
This application for waiver relates to the Boulder Creek Wind Farm Project (**BCWF Project**) and a proposal by Aula Energy Holdings Pty Ltd as trustee for the Aula Energy Asset Hold Trust (**Aula Energy**) to acquire the remaining 50% of the BCWF Project that it does not already own (the **Acquisition**).

Aula Energy is a renewable energy developer and wholesale supplier of electricity. Aula Energy has operated since 2023 and is wholly owned by funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management, an operating group of Macquarie Group Limited.

The BCWF Project involves the development, construction, ownership and operation of a wind farm at Boulder Creek, located approximately 40 km southwest of Rockhampton and 5 km west of Mt Morgan in central Queensland. The BCWF Project is under construction and will supply electricity on a wholesale basis to the National Electricity Market upon completion, the first stage of which is currently anticipated to occur by November 2027.

The BCWF Project is an unincorporated joint venture in which entities in the Aula Energy and CS Energy corporate groups presently hold 50-50 participating interests. CS Energy’s interest in the BCWF Project is held by an entity called BCWF 2 Pty Ltd (**BCWF2**).

The Acquisition involves BCWF 2 Holdings Pty Ltd, a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Aula Energy, acquiring all of the issued share capital in BCWF2 from CS Energy Limited pursuant to a Share Sale and Purchase Deed which the parties expect to execute shortly. The Acquisition will increase Aula Energy’s ownership of the BCWF Project from 50% to 100%.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. post-Acquisition, Aula Energy’s share in the supply of
wholesale electricity generation in the NEM, including in
Queensland, is estimated to be low and the increase in share
of supply arising from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of wholesale electricity
generation in the NEM, including in Queensland.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
